title: Retrograde IO compatibility and parameter aliasing spec
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Define and operationalize a backward-compatibility contract for pinned model versions covering prompt formats, output shapes, parameter semantics (aliases/deprecations), and published performance profiles. This ticket produces a machine-readable manifest, runtime checks for enforcement at ingress, onboarding validation tooling, and guidance for release owners when model changes touch compatibility boundaries.
background: Customers pin model versions for stable behavior. Past incidents showed small parameter renames and subtle output shape changes caused regressions for pinned deployments and customer applications. We need a prescriptive contract so onboarding, Dedicated, and Private deployments can guarantee behavioral and performance invariants for a pinned release.
proposal_summary: Create a three-part contract: 1) IO schema (prompt shapes, required/optional fields, structured output schemas, and example corpora), 2) Parameter compatibility rules (alias table, deprecations, allowed semantic changes), and 3) Performance profile publishing (p90 latency, throughput points, memory/KV cache invariants). Implement an onboarding validator that emits warnings/failures and a runtime compatibility gate that can block incompatible model swaps for pinned versions.
scope: Produce JSON manifest spec + validator CLI + CI check for model onboarding + runtime ingress compatibility gate + docs for PMs/Release owners. Does not include kernel-level perf tuning changes or automatic parameter remapping at runtime (out of scope for this ticket).
design_decisions: Tiered compatibility model: STRICT | SOFT_COMPAT | ADVISORY. STRICT rejects any change that alters required fields or output tokenization from the pinned manifest.
Accept parameter aliases via an explicit alias map in the manifest instead of runtime heuristics to avoid silent behavior changes.
Require a minimal example corpus and a small regression eval (10–50 prompts) for every pinned release that exercises edge output shapes and special tokens.
Publish performance profile as a small table (seq_len x batch_size -> p50/p90 latency and tokens/sec) rather than a single aggregated metric to aid routing and autoscaling decisions.
Enforce compatibility at admission: onboarding pipeline runs validator + regression eval; the runtime gate checks manifest version and blocks incompatible variants when 'pinned' flag is set.
Avoid automatic translation of old prompts to new shapes in this ticket — that will be handled as a separate migration tool if needed.
Favor explicitness over permissiveness. Silent compatibility is the primary cause of customer regressions.
tradeoffs: Strict enforcement reduces accidental regressions but increases onboarding friction for model teams (more PR iterations).
Alias tables and explicit manifests require more authoring work from model owners but give predictable behavior for customers pinning versions.
Publishing richer performance profiles increases maintenance burden but enables better routing and Dedicated capacity planning.
Runtime gate adds latency on rollout checks; we mitigate with cached manifest lookups and async evaluation for non-blocking flows where safe.
This ticket stops short of automated prompt shape adapters which could smooth transitions but are complex and risk hiding regressions.
We rely on a small regression eval — risk of undercoverage; mitigation: require owners to include targeted edge-case prompts and a change log detailing semantic deltas.
acceptance_criteria: A JSON manifest schema is defined and documented in the onboarding Confluence page.
Validator CLI accepts a model artifact bundle and returns PASS/WARN/FAIL with actionable messages.
CI check in the model-onboarding pipeline rejects releases marked as STRICT if validator returns FAIL.
Runtime ingress compatibility gate can block deployments that would replace a pinned model with an incompatible variant (configurable by project).
A minimal regression harness that runs on PRs is added and runs within CI quotas (configurable sample size).
Documentation for PMs and Release owners describing compatibility tiers, alias rules, and performance profile reporting format is published.
Integration smoke-test: deploy a pinned model with a manifest, attempt a semantics-breaking change, and observe expected FAIL path and helpful failure message in the console and CI logs.
tasks: Add CI hook to onboarding pipeline and test against existing pinned releases (Infra)
Build runtime compatibility gate prototype using manifest cache (Runtime team)
Create regression eval harness and sample prompt sets (Applied ML)
Write docs and onboarding checklist for release owners (Product)
Run dogfood on two internal pinned models for one release cycle and capture feedback (Eng)
Finalize alias mapping UX for model owners in the Console (Design + Console)
Security review of manifest format and validator (Security)
Rollout plan and telemetry: track validator failures, customer-facing incidents reduced, and onboarding time delta (Analytics)

risks: Undercoverage in regression harness allows regressions to slip through; mitigation: require owners to include targeted edge-case prompts and expand sampling over time.
Model teams may resist additional authoring overhead; mitigation: provide templates and CLI helpers to generate alias maps and example corpora.
Compatibility gate misconfiguration could block legitimate safe patches; mitigation: add bypass with audit trail and canary modes before strict enforcement.
notes: Prototype validator uses JSON Schema + custom checks for tokenization-preserving transforms.
We will iterate on the alias format to support nested parameter namespaces (eg. 'decode.max_new_tokens' -> 'max_tokens').
Follow-up ticket planned for automated prompt adapters and a migration assistant (separate scope).
